## REASONING

**Goals.** The request "study runoff generation in the Naches" decomposes into (1) a *mechanistic* goal — how runoff partitions between fast surface runoff (QOVER) and slower subsurface drainage/recharge (QDRAI), and how that partitioning is controlled by elevation (via orographic precip and snowpack) and soil texture; and (2) an implied *validation* goal against the only observation offered, USGS stream gauges.

**Feasibility — this is the crux.** Runoff *generation at a column* (QOVER, QDRAI, snowmelt timing) is exactly what single-column ELM produces, and with NLDAS-2 the ~1625 m relief will give genuinely different precip/temperature and a real rain–snow gradient across columns. That part is answerable. **But the validation target — a USGS stream gauge — is integrated basin discharge, and the stack has no lateral routing or aggregation.** Independent 1-D columns cannot be summed into a hydrograph without an explicit routing/aggregation step that does not yet exist. So streamflow validation is *not* feasible as posed; I flag it. Additionally, QDRAI/recharge are slow states — the design must use the WTD-informed warm start (or spin-up), or drainage is an initialization artifact.

**Column locations.** The user gave three points. One, **(46.62, −119.90)**, lies well EAST of the domain bbox (lon −121.5…−120.5) — it is outside HUC 17030002, in the low, dry Columbia Basin, and will get a different NLDAS cell and climate. I retain it as the user requested but flag it as out-of-domain (it can serve as a dry-valley end-member, not a Naches column). The other two — (46.85, −121.05) high near the Cascade crest (snow-dominated) and (47.02, −120.88) mid-elevation — anchor the elevation/snow gradient. To actually *resolve* the two candidate drivers I add a few exploratory columns spanning elevation bands × dominant soils, concentrating in the rain-snow transition where partitioning is most sensitive.

**Drivers feasibility.** Elevation acting through orographic precip and snow IS represented (NLDAS varies with location; SWE is in default output) — so elevation is partially answerable here, unlike a uniform-forcing case. Sub-12 km terrain and ridgetop SWE remain under-resolved. Soil (SSURGO) is a clean lever.
